title: Joining Piron's band in 1928 after Robichaux
summary: Playing for Robichaux, he impressed Cottrell's circle and replaced Paul Barbarin when Barbarin left.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel

blocks.x: Oh, yeah. Did you ever go see, uh, Cuttrell play, you know, with Piran?
Oh, yeah, last time. We played against one, yeah.
They were, all, the Piran band mostly was engaged at Tranchina's nightclub out there, the old Spanish folk.
And, uh, what made me get into the Piran band was the carnival day of 1928, I believe it was. I was playing at the New Orleans Country Club, it was an open house.
And I was doing that time, I was working with John Robichaud band, Professor Robichaud. And that day, they always used two bands on the outside porch.

Each band played the tones. Yeah. So, Paul Barber and this had came back in the air with, from New York. He was, after the old, our country had died. Mm-hmm. Well, Paul Barber was playing drums with him. And when they heard me, what? They all like, they said I played similar like the old man, you see?

So, when Paul was getting ready to leave the band, they sent for me, you see? In fact, Paul told me, they want me to work with people on the band, because he's going to leave and go make up a band with Sonny Allen and, uh, Sonny Allen and Walter Pichon, and they call it the Pelican Silvertone, obviously.
That's Sonny Allen. That'd be Red Allen.

The trumpet player, that's Red Allen. That's Red Allen from Al Jays. We played together too. I forgot to mention him. Way back, we played all this. During the time, right after Lost, Lost, Bush Hall, that's right. But you mentioned Red Allen. We played, he played lots of jobs with our band.
